extracted.intended_audience: readers, librarians, and researchers interested in short fiction anthologies (especially The Best American series)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the editorial selection process and eligibility scope for The Best American Short Stories anthology (1999), including the roles of the series editor and guest editor and the geographic/source limits (U.S. and Canadian magazines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Series mission — showcase the country's finest short fiction and nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Best American series is the premier annual showcase for the country's finest short fiction and nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the series as aiming to collect exemplary work each year; implies selection favors what editors consider 'finest' in craft, originality, and impact, though specific literary criteria are not enumerated on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series editor selection of notable works
rubrics_metrics.description: Each volume's series editor selects notable works from hundreds of periodicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series editor acts as the first-stage filter, surveying a wide range of magazines and identifying 'notable' pieces for consideration. The page does not define 'notable' further (e.g., literary quality, originality, publication prominence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest editor final selection (~20 pieces)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special guest editor, a leading writer in the field, then chooses the best twenty or so pieces to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guest editor (an established writer) makes the final curatorial decision, selecting roughly 20 pieces for inclusion. The page emphasizes the guest editor's authority and taste but provides no explicit scoring rubric or selection criteria beyond 'best.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Source/eligibility scope — works from U.S. and Canadian magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected from U.S. and Canadian magazines (as indicated by the title and metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the geographic/publication eligibility for pieces considered for inclusion: material originally published in magazines from the United States and Canada. The page does not list other eligibility details (e.g., publication year, author residency).
